_about: When trains start on Sundays, and days DMRC announces its own timings for. build.py copies this into data.json's meta.service; index.html applies it when it picks the day's timetable. Times are IST, HH:MM, and are departures from a route's first stop. Every value needs a dated source; leave a line out rather than guess.

sunday_first._about: First departures on Sundays. Lines not listed keep the feed's first trains (05:30-06:00 on most lines), which matches DMRC's 06:00 'regular commencement'. Airport, Rapid Metro and Aqua are left out: no source gives their Sunday start.
sources: DMRC via ANI, Oneindia 6 Nov 2026 ('Delhi Metro revises timings for Diwali 2026'): Pink, Magenta (both corridors) and Grey 'normally commence at 7:00 AM on Sundays'

PTI via ThePrint and india.com, 23 Aug 2024: from 25 Aug 2024 the Phase 3 sections of Lines 1, 3, 5 and 6 (Red, Blue, Green, Violet) start at 06:00 on Sundays, and 'all other corridors ... continue to run as per regular commencement time of 06:00 AM'

special_days._about: Dates (the service day, which runs to 03:00 the next morning) with DMRC-announced timings. timetable: which timetable runs (wkd, sat or sun); a public holiday that DMRC says runs Sunday service is just {"timetable": "sun"}. first: no departure before this time, either one time or per line. last: no departure after this time. Only cuts trains, never adds them.

2026-03-04.name: Holi
2026-03-04.source: DMRC advisory via Business Today, 3 Mar 2026: on Holi, services on all lines including Airport begin at 2:30 PM from terminal stations, then run to the usual timetable

2026-11-08.name: Diwali
2026-11-08.source: DMRC via ANI, Oneindia 6 Nov 2026: Pink, Magenta and Grey start at 6:00 AM instead of 7:00; last train 10:00 PM from terminals on all lines including Airport, instead of 11:00 PM
